precedents.court: Supreme Court of the United States
precedents.keyRule: To survive a motion to dismiss, a complaint must contain sufficient factual matter, accepted as true, to state a claim to relief that is plausible on its face.
precedents.exactQuote: Under Ashcroft v. Iqbal, 556 U.S. 662, 678 (2009), to survive a motion to dismiss, a complaint must contain sufficient factual matter, accepted as true, to state a claim to relief that is plausible on its face.

precedents.court: Supreme Court of the United States
precedents.keyRule: Plaintiffs must nudge their claims across the line from conceivable to plausible.
precedents.exactQuote: Because the plaintiffs here have not nudged their claims across the line from conceivable to plausible, their complaint must be dismissed.

precedents.court: Supreme Court of the United States
precedents.keyRule: Summary judgment is mandated against a party who fails to make a showing sufficient to establish the existence of an element essential to that party's case.
precedents.exactQuote: Rule 56(c) mandates the entry of summary judgment, after adequate time for discovery and upon motion, against a party who fails to make a showing sufficient to establish the existence of an element essential to that party's case.

precedents.caseName: Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
precedents.court: Supreme Court of the United States
precedents.keyRule: Trial judge must ensure that any and all scientific testimony or evidence admitted is not only relevant, but reliable.
precedents.exactQuote: Under the Rules the trial judge must ensure that any and all scientific testimony or evidence admitted is not only relevant, but reliable.

precedents.court: Federal Rules of Evidence Advisory Committee
precedents.keyRule: Certified Records Generated by an Electronic Process or System: A record generated by an electronic process or system that produces an accurate result, as shown by a certification of a qualified person.
precedents.exactQuote: A record generated by an electronic process or system that produces an accurate result, as shown by a certification of a qualified person that complies with the certification requirements of Rule 902(11) or (12).

precedents.court: Federal Rules of Evidence Advisory Committee
precedents.keyRule: Certified Data Copied from an Electronic Device, Storage Medium, or File: Data copied from an electronic device, storage medium, or file, if authenticated by a process of digital identification, as shown by a certification of a qualified person.
precedents.exactQuote: Data copied from an electronic device, storage medium, or file, if authenticated by a process of digital identification, as shown by a certification of a qualified person that complies with the certification requirements of Rule 902(11) or (12).

precedents.court: Supreme Court of the United States
precedents.keyRule: An investment contract for purposes of the Securities Act means a contract, transaction or scheme whereby a person invests his money in a common enterprise and is led to expect profits solely from the efforts of the promoter or a third party.
precedents.exactQuote: An investment contract for purposes of the Securities Act means a contract, transaction or scheme whereby a person invests his money in a common enterprise and is led to expect profits solely from the efforts of the promoter or a third party.

precedents.court: Supreme Court of the United States
precedents.keyRule: Notes are presumed to be securities unless they bear a strong family resemblance to non-security commercial instruments under the four-factor Reves test.
precedents.exactQuote: A note is presumed to be a security, and that presumption may be rebutted only by a showing that the note bears a strong resemblance to one of the enumerated categories of instrument.

precedents.court: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York
precedents.keyRule: Programmatic sales of tokens on digital asset exchanges to blind public buyers did not constitute offers and sales of investment contracts under Howey.
precedents.exactQuote: Having considered the economic reality and totality of circumstances, the Court concludes that XRP, as a digital token, is not in and of itself a 'contract, transaction or scheme' that embodies the Howey requirements of an investment contract.

precedents.caseName: In re Caremark Int'l Inc. Derivative Litig.
precedents.keyRule: Directors have an affirmative duty to attempt in good faith to assure that a corporate information and reporting system exists.
precedents.exactQuote: A sustained or systematic failure of the board to exercise oversight—such as an utter failure to attempt to assure a reasonable information and reporting system exists—will establish the lack of good faith that is a necessary condition to liability.

precedents.keyRule: Board must make a good faith effort to implement and monitor an oversight system for central, mission-critical compliance operations.
precedents.exactQuote: When a board fails to make any good faith effort to put in place a reasonable board-level system of monitoring and reporting regarding mission-critical risks, it breaches its duty of loyalty.

precedents.court: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York (Castel, J.)
precedents.keyRule: Sanctions imposed under Rule 11 for citing non-existent judicial decisions with bogus citations and quotes generated by ChatGPT.
precedents.exactQuote: Many harms flow from the submission of fake opinions. The opposing party wastes time and money in exposing the deception. The court's time is taken from other matters. A fabricated opinion is a lie told to a court of law.

precedents.citation: ABA Standing Comm. on Ethics & Prof. Resp., Formal Op. 512 (2024)
precedents.keyRule: Lawyers using Generative AI tools must verify the accuracy of all citations and legal propositions, ensure client confidentiality, and maintain independent attorney supervision under Model Rules 1.1, 1.6, 3.3, and 5.1/5.3.
precedents.exactQuote: Because GAI outputs can be inaccurate, incomplete, or biased, lawyers may not rely on GAI tool outputs without independent verification by human counsel.

precedents.caseName: Alice Corp. Pty. Ltd. v. CLS Bank Int'l
precedents.court: Supreme Court of the United States
precedents.keyRule: Two-step framework for patent eligibility under 35 U.S.C. § 101: determine if claims are directed to a patent-ineligible concept, then search for an inventive concept sufficient to transform the idea into a patent-eligible application.
precedents.exactQuote: We must first determine whether the claims at issue are directed to a patent-ineligible concept, such as an abstract idea. If so, we then ask: what else is there in the claims before us?
